strengths: Addresses a genuinely underexplored problem in V2A generation: physical grounding of generated sounds with respect to object mass and velocity, rather than purely appearance-driven audio-visual correlation.

The proposed pipeline (PPE + Phy-Adapter) is reasonably well-engineered, combining VLM-based mass estimation, open-vocabulary segmentation, and dynamic 3D reconstruction for metric-scale velocity, and integrates physics cues via a residual delta-modulation mechanism that is shown to outperform naive summation in ablations.

New benchmark (VGG-Impact) and new metric (APCC) are useful contributions toward more rigorous evaluation of physical plausibility in V2A, addressing a real gap in existing perceptual/semantic metrics.

Quantitative results across a wide range of baselines (9 models) show consistent improvements on both perceptual metrics (FD, KL, IS, IB-score, DeSync) and the proposed APCC-Delta metric, and the ablation study isolates the contribution of mass vs. velocity conditioning and modulation strategy.
A user study with physical plausibility ratings supports the quantitative claims and shows PAVAS is rated favorably compared to baselines on multiple perceptual axes.
weaknesses: The accuracy of the core physics estimators (mass from VLM, velocity from monocular dynamic 3D reconstruction) is only briefly asserted ("comparable to, or even surpassing, specialized expert models") with details deferred entirely to supplementary material not included here; without seeing this validation in the main paper, the central premise that these physics estimates are reliable enough to condition generation is not verifiable from the manuscript body alone.

Monocular metric-scale velocity/mass estimation from single video, especially via VLM text-based reasoning, is inherently noisy and possibly scene/camera-scale ambiguous; no uncertainty quantification or failure-case analysis is presented in the main text to characterize how estimation errors propagate to audio quality.

The APCC metric itself depends on the same imperfect PPE-derived physical quantities (kinetic energy from estimated mass/velocity) to evaluate physical consistency, creating a potential circularity: a model conditioned on PPE outputs may naturally correlate better with PPE-derived ground truth than models that never see such signals, which could bias the benchmark in favor of the proposed method.

VGG-Impact benchmark is relatively small (272 impact moments, 10 classes) and manually curated by the authors, raising questions about selection bias and statistical robustness of the reported APCC differences; no confidence intervals or significance tests accompany Table 1.

Backbone parameter/architecture comparisons are somewhat uneven (only Large variants of MMAudio and PAVAS run at 44.1kHz while baselines run at 16kHz), which could confound perceptual quality metrics like FD/IS beyond the physics-conditioning contribution.

The user study is modest in scale (15 participants, 8 audio samples) which limits the statistical power of the subjective evaluation, and no significance testing is reported for the differences in Table 2.

The system relies on several large pretrained modules (VLM, Grounded-SAM2, CUT3R) chained together, and the paper does not report runtime/inference cost overhead relative to baselines, which is relevant for practical usefulness given the added complexity for a modest quantitative gain over MMAudio-L in several metrics (e.g., FD_VGG, KL_PANNs where MMAudio is comparable or better).

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and underexplored gap in V2A generation: existing models are appearance-driven and ignore explicit physical dynamics (mass, velocity) that shape real-world sound.

Proposes a full, well-engineered pipeline (PPE + Phy-Adapter with FiLM modulation and a delta-modulation residual injection mechanism) that is compatible with a modern multimodal diffusion transformer backbone, and shows via ablation that each physics stream (mass, velocity) and the residual injection strategy contribute measurable gains over a longer-trained backbone baseline.

Introduces a new benchmark (VGG-Impact) and a new interpretable metric (APCC) targeting physical plausibility, which is a genuine methodological contribution beyond standard perceptual/semantic V2A metrics.

Extensive empirical validation: quantitative comparison against 8 strong baselines, a 27-participant user study with consistent gains including on the newly introduced physical-plausibility dimension, and substantial supplementary analyses (mass/velocity estimator validation against expert baselines, sensitivity/robustness to perturbed or missing physics cues, runtime profiling, generalization beyond impact-centric scenes).

Reasonable design choices for open-world generalization (VLM-based mass reasoning, open-vocabulary segmentation + dynamic 3D reconstruction for metric-scale velocity) rather than requiring calibrated multi-view setups as in prior mass-estimation work.

Qualitative spectrogram comparisons and supplementary video convincingly illustrate cases (goad honking, golf driving, dog barking, wood chopping) where PAVAS avoids duplicated/misaligned/overextended acoustic events compared to baselines.
weaknesses: Potential evaluation bias in APCC: the same PPE used to condition PAVAS is also used to derive the reference kinetic-energy signal for the metric, meaning PAVAS is directly optimized toward correlating with the exact signal used for its own evaluation, which could inflate its advantage over baselines independent of true physical realism; a more independent physics ground truth (e.g., sensor-based or simulation-based) would strengthen the claim.

The physical model used is quite coarse: a single time-invariant scalar mass plus centroid-based translational velocity ignores material stiffness/elasticity, contact geometry, rotational motion, and resonance properties that strongly determine real impact sounds, so the 'physics-aware' claim is somewhat narrower than the framing suggests (acknowledged as future work but still a substantive limitation).
VGG-Impact benchmark is relatively small after filtering (272 impact moments across 10 classes), limiting the statistical robustness of the APCC-based comparisons.

Mass and velocity estimator validations rely on proxy benchmarks (ABO-500 for static multi-view objects, STARSS23 with a pseudo-ground-truth pipeline for velocity) that may not fully represent the dynamic, in-the-wild VGGSound/VGG-Impact conditions where PAVAS is actually deployed, so estimator reliability in the target domain is not directly verified against real ground truth.

Gains on some standard distributional/perceptual metrics over the strongest baseline (MMAudio-L) are modest or mixed (e.g., FD_VGG and KL_PANNs are comparable or slightly worse), so improvements are concentrated in physics-consistency measures rather than uniformly across all axes.

The pipeline depends on multiple heavy pretrained modules (VLM, Grounded-SAM2, CUT3R) with CUT3R dominating runtime, raising practical concerns about inference cost and scalability that are noted but not resolved.

Presentation is dense with many symbols/equations in the main text; some architectural details (e.g., precise interaction between object-centric features and multimodal condition) require cross-referencing the supplementary material to fully follow.
